title: Binance hack: developing story
summary: The largest crypto theft on record: on Oct 29 attackers moved about US$6.3 billion (Binance's estimate) out of Binance's own hot wallets on 10 blockchains. About US$3 billion has been frozen. Binance said on Nov 1 that about 95% of the stolen amount has been replenished from company funds (up from about 90% on Oct 31) and in a Nov 1 notice set the first phase of the withdrawal restart for 06:00 to 09:00 UTC Sunday (1 to 4 a.m. ET, after the clocks go back), network by network. It plans a full proof of reserves by Monday, Nov 2.

facts.label: Stolen
facts.note: Binance's own estimate of the impact (Reuters); TRM Labs: about US$6.36B moved out of Binance wallets on 10 blockchains; Chainalysis's Jonathan Levin put it at US$6.4B in a later update (Cointelegraph, 05:01 UTC Oct 30)
facts.source: Reuters via Investing.com; Cointelegraph live updates

facts.label: Frozen so far
facts.note: Binance said verified frozen assets reached about US$3B (00:52 UTC Oct 30), including more than US$1.567B USDT frozen by Tether and more than US$800M USDC by Circle; First Digital froze the FDUSD involved

facts.label: Still with the attacker
facts.note: Bitquery's count of the attacker's wallets, mostly ether and bitcoin (06:43 UTC Oct 30; Euronews reported US$3.1B from an earlier count). A different measure, TRM Labs' funds 'beyond the reach of token issuers', was about US$2.4B (00:30 UTC Oct 30). Stolen, frozen and still held come from different sources and times, so they need not add up

facts.label: Recovered
facts.value: about 95% of the stolen amount replenished (Binance, Nov 1); no recovered amount published
facts.note: Binance said on Nov 1 that about 95% of the impacted amount is now covered, up from about 90% on Oct 31, with less-liquid tokens outside the top 10 making up the remaining 5% (The Defiant; Business Today; Coinpedia). It has begun recovering frozen funds but has not said how much has come back

facts.label: When
facts.note: most of the money left within about 20 minutes (TRM Labs; Yahoo Finance), and the attacker kept moving funds out of 17 hot wallets until about 7:56 p.m. ET (Bitquery, via Euronews). The first public signs came about an hour after it began: Changpeng Zhao's post at about 5:15 p.m. ET, then Binance's statement

facts.label: Who
facts.value: North Korea's TraderTraitor, a Lazarus-linked unit (TRM Labs and Chainalysis assessments)
facts.note: TRM Labs assessed it with 'high confidence' and Chainalysis reached the same conclusion; Binance says its own investigation has not attributed it to anyone, no government has formally attributed it yet (as of Oct 30), and North Korea routinely denies such attacks

facts.label: Binance
facts.value: deposits working normally; withdrawals restarting in stages: Binance's Nov 1 notice put the first phase between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC Sunday (1 to 4 a.m. ET, after the clocks go back), network by network after security checks, starting with 15 networks including Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Tron and Solana; proof-of-reserves results by Monday, Nov 2; says it will cover all losses with company funds
facts.note: Preliminary finding: a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop let an attacker reach a service container that could submit withdrawal transactions; no evidence of a private-key leak. Binance later found additional points of breach: co-CEO Richard Teng said on Oct 30 the attackers used a self-destruct mechanism to erase their tools and traces and used EIP-7702 to gain execution authority over one hot wallet, bypassing the usual approvals, and that the attack hit Binance's own hot wallet, not customer funds. Binance has reserved more than US$6.34B, US$5B of it already held in the affected assets, the rest being bought on the market and over the counter. Binance.US not affected.
facts.source: Cointelegraph and CNBC (Oct 31); Binance notice on X (via TokenPost, Bloomingbit); CoinDesk; Decrypt; Bloomingbit (Oct 31, 9:20 p.m. PT); CryptoTicker (Nov 1, 04:46 UTC)
